newsitem.title: CHINA: Asian growth "miracle" losing shine - consultant.
newsitem.headline: Asian growth "miracle" losing shine - consultant.

text.p: The Asian economic "miracle" may be wearing thin and be in need of re-assessment with growth in many parts of the continent slowing, Fred Steingraber, head of consultancy firm A.T. Kearney said on Wednesday.

Steingraber, whose company is hosting its global business policy forum in Shanghai this week, said investors needed to be cautious given the problems many Asian countries were experiencing in maintaining and building on a fast development pace.
"There are things happening which make people question how long we can keep this Asian growth miracle thing going," Steingraber said in an interview.
"Long-term there is clearly significant potential for development in growth rates, but at the same time there are a lot of hurdles that Asia faces," he added.
Steingraber said Japan's economy still appeared stalled, Korea looking less rosy than last year, and Thailand was beset with problems. Foreign investment into China appeared to be slowing, he said.
Infrastructure problems, inconsistencies in legal and accounting practices, and intellectual property rights infringements were just some of the issues making Asia problematic for investors, he said.
"Until they sort these out, the ability to sustain the attraction of capital from places other than Japan will be tricky," he said.
